about: Reclaim grade table. Copper-family grades are a band of the copper reference price (ratio low-high); other metals are fixed USD/lb bands. Every band names its source and the date it was checked. These are estimates of what US scrap yards pay; your local yard will differ.

fallback.license: Single price fact quoted with attribution.

mc-copper.name: MetalCharts: scrap copper prices
mc-copper.note: Estimated yard ranges as a share of COMEX, checked against posted yard boards (Rockaway Recycling NJ, Central Metal Recycling Chicago, MetalRecap survey, ScrapMonster spreads).

mc-metals.name: MetalCharts: scrap metal prices
mc-metals.note: Estimated yard ranges, checked against posted yard boards.

mc-brass.name: MetalCharts: scrap brass prices
mc-brass.note: Estimated yard ranges as a share of COMEX copper.

mc-aluminum.name: MetalCharts: scrap aluminum prices
mc-aluminum.note: Estimated yard ranges against LME aluminum.

mc-motors.name: MetalCharts: electric motor scrap prices
mc-motors.note: Flat bands from September 2026 yard boards.

sm-escrap.name: ScrapMonster yard price listing
sm-escrap.note: Single quoted prices; Reclaim shows a plus or minus 20% band around them.

derived.name: Reclaim estimate (derived)
derived.note: No public band found. Derived from a sourced grade as stated in the basis line. Treat as low confidence and get a yard quote.

grades.name: Bare bright copper
grades.basis: MetalCharts estimated yard range, as a share of COMEX
grades.notes: Clean, shiny, unalloyed bare wire 16 ga or thicker. No tarnish, solder, paint or insulation.

grades.name: #1 copper (heavy, clean tubing, bus bar)
grades.basis: MetalCharts estimated yard range, as a share of COMEX
grades.notes: Clean unalloyed pipe, tubing, bus bar and clippings with no solder, fittings or paint.

grades.name: #2 copper (soldered pipe, oxidized wire)
grades.basis: MetalCharts estimated yard range, as a share of COMEX
grades.notes: Pipe with solder or fittings, painted or tarnished wire, about 96% copper.

grades.name: Light copper (#3: sheet, gutters, flashing)
grades.basis: MetalCharts estimated yard range, as a share of COMEX
grades.notes: Thin sheet, roofing, gutters, downspouts. Remove nails and tar.

grades.name: Magnet wire (enamelled, clean)
grades.basis: Derived: MetalCharts notes yards usually buy enamelled magnet wire as #2 copper; band set at or slightly under #2
grades.notes: Motor and transformer windings once cut out. Spools and steel cores must be removed.

grades.name: #1 insulated (85%+ copper: heavy single conductor)
grades.basis: Derived: 85-92% recovery x bare-bright band x 0.85 processing factor (calibrated on MetalCharts THHN, Romex and low-grade bands)
grades.notes: Thick single-conductor wire with thin insulation, 6 AWG and larger. No connectors.

grades.name: THHN / THWN building wire (about 78%)
grades.basis: MetalCharts THHN and high-grade insulated band, 52-62% of COMEX
grades.notes: Single conductors with thin nylon jacket. Stripping 10 AWG and up usually pays; small gauges rarely do.

grades.name: Romex / NM-B house wire (about 65%)
grades.basis: MetalCharts Romex and house wire band, 42-50% of COMEX
grades.notes: Jacketed cable with a bare ground. Cut off boxes and devices.

grades.name: #2 insulated (about 48%: cords, harnesses)
grades.basis: MetalCharts low-grade insulated band (appliance cords, car harnesses), 26-34% of COMEX
grades.notes: Extension and appliance cords, mixed harnesses. Plugs cut off pays more at some yards.

grades.name: Low-grade insulated (about 25%)
grades.basis: Derived: 20-30% recovery x bare-bright band x 0.85 processing factor
grades.notes: Thin cords with heavy jackets, data cables with shielding, wire with steel messenger.

grades.name: Communication wire (Cat5/6, phone)
grades.basis: Derived: 30-40% recovery (eight 24 AWG conductors in a jacket) x bare-bright band x 0.85
grades.notes: Copper-clad aluminium (CCA) network cable is NOT copper and pays far less. Coax with a steel core pays less.

grades.name: Christmas lights
grades.basis: Derived: 15-30% recovery x bare-bright band x 0.85; many yards cap or refuse lights
grades.notes: Call first. Some yards only take them in season or by the gaylord.

grades.name: Clean ACR / Al-Cu coil (no steel)
grades.basis: MetalCharts aluminum/copper coil band, 34-42% of COMEX
grades.notes: Condenser and evaporator coils with copper tube and aluminum fins, steel end plates removed. Refrigerant must be recovered first.

grades.name: Dirty ACR (steel ends attached)
grades.basis: Derived: 60-70% of the clean ACR band for attached steel and brackets
grades.notes: Cutting the steel ends off usually moves it up to clean ACR.

grades.name: Copper/brass radiators (auto, truck)
grades.basis: MetalCharts copper and brass radiator band, 36-47% of COMEX
grades.notes: Drained, plastic tanks and steel brackets removed. Aluminium radiators are priced like cast/sheet aluminium.

grades.name: Yellow brass (fittings, valves, fixtures)
grades.basis: MetalCharts yellow brass band, 41-50% of COMEX
grades.notes: Plumbing fittings, valves, faucet bodies. Remove steel and plastic.

grades.name: Red brass / bronze (valves, water meters)
grades.basis: MetalCharts red brass and bronze band, 47-62% of COMEX
grades.notes: Gunmetal valves and bronze castings. Water meters can be utility property: provenance matters.

grades.name: Aluminum: clean extrusion (6063)
grades.basis: MetalCharts clean 6063 extrusion band
grades.notes: Window frames, rails. No glass, rubber, steel screws or paint.

grades.name: Aluminum: sheet, cast, cans
grades.basis: MetalCharts sheet ($0.55-0.66), cast ($0.48-0.59) and UBC ($0.50-0.61) bands combined
grades.notes: Separate grades pay more than mixed.

grades.name: Steel: heavy melt / prepared
grades.basis: MetalCharts prepared steel / HMS No.1 band; mill programs reprice about monthly
grades.notes: Thick structural steel cut to size. Regional spread is wide; yards quote per gross ton.

grades.name: Light iron (appliances, tin, sheet)
grades.basis: MetalCharts light iron and unprepared steel band
grades.notes: Appliance shells, sheet, bed frames.

grades.name: Stainless steel 304
grades.basis: MetalCharts 304 stainless band (keyed to LME nickel)
grades.notes: Non-magnetic. Sinks, restaurant equipment. 316 pays roughly double.

grades.name: Electric motors: small, whole
grades.basis: MetalCharts small electric motor band (fan, pump, appliance, power tool)
grades.notes: Copper-wound sells better than aluminum-wound; cut-out windings sell as #2 copper.

grades.name: Electric motors: large / industrial
grades.basis: Derived: small-motor band shifted up for the higher copper share of large copper-wound motors; yards grade these separately, so ask
grades.notes: Working industrial motors often resell for far more than scrap: check resale first.

grades.name: Alternators & starters
grades.basis: MetalCharts alternators and starters band
grades.notes: Whole units.

grades.name: Sealed units / compressors
grades.basis: MetalCharts sealed units and compressors band (oil drained)
grades.notes: Fridge and AC compressors. Oil drained; most yards want proof the refrigerant was recovered.

grades.name: Transformers (copper-wound, dry)
grades.basis: Derived: most yards price small dry transformers like whole motors (MetalCharts motor band); aluminium-wound pays less
grades.notes: Oil-filled units may contain PCBs: do not cut or drain, and ask the yard first. Utility pole transformers are almost never legitimately for sale.

grades.name: Lead-acid batteries
grades.basis: MetalCharts car and truck battery band (keyed to LME lead)
grades.notes: Keep upright, intact, not leaking.

grades.name: Circuit boards (high grade)
grades.basis: ScrapMonster listing 2026-08-11: high-grade board $1.25/lb, shown as a plus or minus 20% band
grades.notes: Gold-finger memory and CPU boards are graded separately; low-grade (TV, appliance) boards pay far less.

grades.name: E-scrap: whole computers / servers
grades.basis: ScrapMonster listing 2026-08-11: computer/server complete $0.25/lb, shown as a plus or minus 20% band
grades.notes: CRT monitors and TVs usually cost money to drop off.

grades.name: Non-recoverable (plastic, wood, glass, oil)
grades.basis: No scrap value; counts toward weight and disposal
grades.notes: Budget a dump fee for this fraction under disposal.
